title: Cultural Adaptation, Validation, and Evaluation of the Programme for Promotion of Healthy Affective-Sexual Behaviours in Adolescents (IYG)
official: Protocol for a Mixed Methods Study of the Cultural Adaptation, Validation, and Evaluation of It's Your Game: Keep It Real for the Promotion of Healthy Affective and Sexual Behaviours in Spain
summary:
This study aims to adapt and evaluate \*It's Your Game: Keep It Real\* (IYG), a school-based sexual health education programme developed in the United States, for adolescents aged 11-14 years in Spain. The adapted programme, Es Tu Juego: Decide Bien\*, will be evaluated in Andalusia and Catalonia.

The project includes cultural adaptation activities involving adolescents, families and professionals, followed by usability testing. These activities will help ensure that the programme is understandable, appropriate and relevant to adolescents in Spain.

The effectiveness of the adapted programme will then be evaluated in a study involving approximately 1,488 adolescents from 16 secondary schools. Schools will be randomly assigned to receive either the programme or their usual educational activities.

IYG consists of two levels of 12 sessions each, combining classroom activities with digital learning. Topics include healthy relationships, sexual decision-making, consent, personal boundaries, contraception and prevention of sexually transmitted infections.

Participants will complete questionnaires at the beginning of the study and after 6, 18 and 24 months. Researchers will assess whether the programme helps delay the initiation of sexual activity and improves sexual health knowledge, attitudes and preventive skills. Schools in the control group will be offered the programme after the final follow-up.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adolescents aged 11-14 years enrolled in the first year of compulsory secondary education (ESO) at baseline.
* Students attending participating secondary schools in Andalusia or Catalonia.
* Sufficient understanding of Spanish or Catalan to complete the study procedures.
* Written informed consent from a parent or legal guardian and verbal assent from the adolescent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Students attending schools that are concurrently implementing structured programmes specifically targeting adolescent sexual risk prevention.
* Inability to complete the intervention or study assessments, even with reasonable accommodations.
